title: Rethinking "dark intelligence": Emotional intelligence as a link between dark triad and interpersonal emotion management.
abstract: Guided by an integrated framework comprising of the trait perspective of personality, trait emotional intelligence (EI) theory and emotion regulation theory, the study explored how dark triad (DT) relates to interpersonal emotion management (IEM) and whether EI explains these associations. Using a sample of industrial managerial staff (N = 242) from industries situated in the city of Guwahati, Assam, India; the study assessed whether EI statistically mediates the links between Machiavellianism, narcissism, psychopathy and five IEM factors - Enhance, Divert, Worsen, Inauthentic and Conceal. Participants completed the Short Dark Triad, Brief Emotional Intelligence Scale and Managing the Emotions of Others Scale - very short form. The results demonstrated that narcissism was positively associated with the prosocial strategies (Enhance and Divert), whereas psychopathy was negatively related to them. All three DT traits were positively associated with the non-prosocial strategies (Worsen and Inauthentic), with psychopathy showing the strongest relationship with Worsen. None of the traits were related to Conceal. Mediation analyses further revealed significant indirect associations through EI between the DT and prosocial IEM factors, but not the non-prosocial factors. Similarly, the indirect associations with Conceal were not significant. In sum, the findings indicate that EI may be associated with constructive emotion management but may not be related to manipulative emotional influence, thus refining the notion of "dark emotional intelligence".
